{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABaoJwOQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhEOvXM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 77, "title": "Implement SH-2 standby and NMI sequencing for Saturn clock changes", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `7a2f68c23bb39a64b8f3ddd4efe90a1205e7d8dd`, clock switching changes the PLL and resets several devices, but does not implement the documented master-CPU lifecycle:

- `src/hle/system.s:152–186` implements SYS_CHGSYSCK by masking interrupts, issuing CKCHG and polling SF. It never enters software standby.
- `src/bus.rs:728–738` resets video, SCU and sound at completion while preserving master on-chip state.
- `src/lib.rs:861–870` handles clock completion without the NMI signaling used by NMIREQ.
- The existing clock bus test explicitly expects the master FRC to remain running. Current guest tests verify final device state and return values, without establishing standby, wake or DMA consequences.

This affects a standard firmware operation used when changing display clocks. Successful final readback does not establish correct behavior while CPUs, DMA and peripherals cross the transition.

## Expected outcome

Implement a specification-derived clock-change lifecycle shared by original external synthetic firmware and BIOS-free HLE. The HLE service must perform its required preparation and recovery through original SH-2 instructions and MMIO. The hardware scheduler must provide the corresponding clock/reset/NMI events through existing CPU and bus mechanisms.

Primary contract:

- [Sega System Program User’s Manual, Guide, “System clock switching”](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/prgg/sysg/prog/hon/p01_10.htm): master standby, FRT/SCI reinitialization, WDT involvement, NMI-related DMAC suspension, reset domains and post-switch recovery.
- [SMPC User’s Manual §2.3, commands 9–10](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/smpc/hon/p02_30.htm): CKCHG352/320 interfaces, completion, device states and firmware-service requirement.
- [SH7604 Hardware Manual §§14.4.1–14.4.5, Table 14.3 and Figures 14.1–14.2; §9.2.7](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/sh7604.pdf): standby entry, register retention/reset, wake timing and DMAOR.NMIF behavior.

Keep firmware responsibilities distinct from hardware effects. Derive the board’s signal sequence rather than treating a generic Hitachi example as proof of Saturn wiring. Separate unspecified oscillator/interface phases from documented behavior using explicit deterministic conventions.

This increment covers clock-change preparation, standby, wake and recovery. It does not complete unrelated reset, CPU, video, sound or peripheral requirements.

## Context and reproduction

Inspect the functions above and run the existing original clock fixtures through `tests/clock.rs` and their production Wasm checks in `scripts/browser-smoke.mjs`. They currently establish completed clock selection, retained execution and selected device resets, but lack the new lifecycle assertions.

Existing reusable mechanisms include `OnChip::enter_sleep`, `OnChip::signal_nmi`, watchdog settling, DMA standby handling and scheduled CPU exception entry. Integrate these mechanisms rather than adding a separate clock-service execution shortcut.

Reconcile primary-source differences explicitly. In particular, SMPC describes Work RAM retention while the System Program guide distinguishes SDRAM from unspecified/destroyed DRAM contents. Do not infer a new low-WRAM clearing rule from that label alone. Document the supported retention contract and any unresolved deviation. Likewise, distinguish intentional HLE recovery from hardware-initialized FRT/SCI/DMA state.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document a primary-referenced stage table covering guest preparation, command acceptance, standby, PLL/device transition, NMI/wake, exception entry and service return. Identify specified ordering, firmware actions and deterministic phase choices. Correct mistaken task assumptions autonomously with exact references and rationale.
- [ ] Replace the HLE’s transition-long SF polling with an original instruction-executed implementation of the documented protocol. Preserve its public ABI, callee saves, caller return state and clock-value interface; reconcile SCU mask/shadow recovery with the System Program contract.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the master retires no instructions and issues no new CPU transactions during standby. Apply Table 14.3 peripheral effects and WDT-selected wake timing; preserve the documented architectural and controller state. Do not manufacture effects only when the HLE service address executes.
- [ ] Deliver the documented clock-change NMI events through the normal input, DMA and exception paths. Independently assert saved PC/SR, handler execution and return, NMIF visibility, DMA inhibition and guest-controlled restart. Verify hot-reset-enable behavior against the cited clock-service specification.
- [ ] Add native boundary vectors before, at and after standby, transition, wake and return. Cover both clock directions, NTSC/PAL clock conversion, pending CPU reads/writes, on-chip DMA phases, slave shutdown and SCU cancellation. Assert completed effects occur once and unfinished work follows the documented cancellation/drain contract.
- [ ] Preserve CD, RTC, backup and supported RAM retention across the transition. Test continued fixed-clock progress while the master is stopped, device reinitialization and successful post-switch video/audio operation. Reset or a second cold boot must not retain stale wake events or transaction journals.
- [ ] Add reproducible MIT-licensed synthetic firmware and an HLE caller fixture with independently authored register/event expectations. Guest instructions must record peripheral reset, DMA inhibition/restart and interrupt-return results. Include changed operands, omitted preparation/restart controls and repeated cold boots. No proprietary BIOS, copied firmware routine or host-written result mailbox is permitted.
- [ ] Execute the same guest bytes and expectations natively and through production browser Wasm under `/saturn-rust/`. Assert guest records, actual Canvas output and deterministic nonzero audio after recovery. Retain browser responsiveness, input/focus and local-file privacy checks.
- [ ] Prove the new lifecycle oracle fails on inherited main for the missing behavior. Verify identical relevant traces across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and passive inspection on/off; do not derive golden values from emulator output.
- [ ] Preserve existing tests and all three demonstrations. Amend an existing expectation only when primary evidence contradicts it, recording the precise correction and retaining its useful coverage. Update architecture, conformance and validation records without marking #17 complete.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target and Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, CI-runner tests and the complete extended `npm run test:browser`, without skipping required checks or weakening publication gates.

All remaining #17 CPU/peripheral, bus/cache/reset/arbitration, SCU/DSP, video/audio/CD timing, media/HLE/SMPC and integrated evidence requirements remain mandatory. Genuine BIOS operation and broad commercial-game compatibility remain unverified. Do not reopen historical trackers or interpret administrative closure as completion.

## Optional validation

None required. Existing lawful commercial compatibility observations may supplement the original fixtures, but are not dependencies.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
